title: Fraction Word Problems
short: Solve stories that add or subtract like fractions.

blocks.html: Stories about rain, rope, juice and distance often use fractions with the same denominator. Use the skills from adding and subtracting mixed numbers; the story tells you which one.

Decide what the story does. Putting amounts together (in all, total, altogether) means add. Taking away, finding what is left, or comparing (how much more, how much farther) means subtract. Then keep the denominator and work with the numerators.

A fraction story is a whole-number story with fraction-sized pieces. "It rained 3 eighths of an inch, then 4 eighths more" is the same as "3 drops, then 4 more drops," only the drops are eighths. A tape diagram shows the parts and the whole.

blocks.name: tapediagram
blocks.cap: Two parts and an unknown total: add.

blocks.title: Put together
blocks.q: It rained $\dfrac{3}{8}$ inch on Monday and $\dfrac{4}{8}$ inch on Tuesday. How much rain fell in all?

blocks.title: What is left
blocks.q: A rope is $5\dfrac{1}{4}$ feet long. Sam cuts off $2\dfrac{3}{4}$ feet. How much rope is left?

blocks.html: Write the unit with your answer. "$2\dfrac{2}{4}$" alone does not say whether it is feet, miles or cups.
